brief: A planter tower for a patio: one planter three storeys tall in the middle, ringed by six planters two storeys tall, with a crescent of five one-storey planters hugging the front of the ring on the side nearest the default view, so the whole build steps up one, two and three storeys away from the viewer. All bins radial-drain. Behind the ring, three one-storey cells with covers make a potting shelf: one small nursery pot on each cover, each filled with soil and planted with a seedling. Fill every planter with soil and plant it: a patio tomato in the middle; butterhead lettuce, oakleaf lettuce, parsley, basil, chives and a marigold around the ring; nasturtium, alyssum, strawberry, thyme and oregano along the crescent. Use look to check that every plant is visible from the default view.

finish.summary: Built a stepped patio planter tower: a three-storey centre planter (patio tomato) ringed by six two-storey radial-drain planters (butterhead, oakleaf, parsley, basil, chives, marigold), a five-planter one-storey crescent (nasturtium, alyssum, strawberry, thyme, oregano) hugging the front on the default-view side, and a three-cell covered potting shelf behind the ring holding three soil-filled nursery pots with basil, parsley and tomato seedlings. All 12 planters are soil-filled hex-bin-full-drain-radial bins, open faces were capped and joints locked, and look confirms all 15 plants are visible from the default view; check_build passes with meshClash clear. One adaptation: the configurator refused a 3-storey-deep bin (NEEDS_TALL_BASE), so the centre uses a standard-depth bin in the top cell of its three-storey stack.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, radial holes
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
